The line segment $\overline{XY}$ is a diameter of a circle. Given that $X$ and $Y$ have coordinates $(-5,-4)$ and $(-1,2)$, respectively, what is the equation of the circle?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is

$$
(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2.
$$

Using the distance formula to compute the distance between the points $X(-5,-4)$ and $Y(-1,2),$ we find that the length of the diameter is

$$
\begin{aligned}XY & =\sqrt{((-5)-(-1))^2+((-4)-2)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^2+(-6)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{16+36} \\  & =\sqrt{52} \\  & =\sqrt{4\cdot 13} \\  & =2\sqrt{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the radius of the circle is

$$
r=\frac{XY}{2}=\frac{2\sqrt{13}}{2}=\sqrt{13}.
$$

Since the center of a circle is the midpoint of the diameter, to find the center we use the midpoint formula as follows:

$$
(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2},\frac{y_1+y_2}{2})=(\frac{-5+(-1)}{2},\frac{-4+2}{2})=(-3,-1)
$$

So our circle has radius $r=\sqrt{13}$ and center $(a,b)=(-3,-1),$ and therefore it is represented by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2 & =r^2 \\ (x-(-3))^{2}+(y-(-1))^{2} & =(\sqrt{13})^2 \\ (x+3)^{2}+(y+1)^{2} & =13\end{aligned}
$$
